modelName: RCN as a network of action situations — the four drawings placed at Ostrom's three levels
modelNote: A NAS (network of action situations) view, after McGinnis: two action situations are adjacent when outcomes generated in one determine a working component, or the rules, of the other. The four boxes with icons are our four VNA drawings, placed at the level of analysis assigned 2026-08-31. Downward arrows are adjacency — an outcome above setting a rule below. The empty constitutional band and the red arrow are the two findings: we have drawn no constitutional arena at all, and the CHW position has no adjacency to the collective-choice arena that sets its payoff. Method is nas, not vna: these arrows are adjacency claims, not deliverables, so the value-network rules correctly do not apply.

nodes.label: Two situations that look like one. One arena nobody has drawn. And a position with no way up.
nodes.note: Everything on this canvas came out of assigning Ostrom's levels to four drawings that were made without any of this in mind.

nodes.label: CONSTITUTIONAL
nodes.note: Who has standing in which choice situation, and which institutional mechanisms are available to them. Ostrom 2005:58-62.

nodes.label: COLLECTIVE-CHOICE
nodes.note: Where actors shape the rules that constrain actors in operational arenas.

nodes.label: OPERATIONAL
nodes.note: Where the choices of actors directly affect tangible outcomes.

nodes.label: WHO MAY ENTER WHICH SEAT
nodes.note: Not one of our four drawings says who may become a mentor, who may sit on a board, or who may hold a CHW position. That is a gap in what we have drawn, not a claim that no such arena exists. Drawing it dashed and empty is the honest move.

nodes.label: CO-OP BOARD
nodes.note: From hybrid-coop-money-and-value. Elects consumer and worker seats, sets the split, and sets PRICE and WAGE — the bigger half, made quietly. Four arrows in that file are collective-choice; the other 23 are operational, which is why it flags as spanning.

nodes.label: PLAN DESIGN
nodes.note: The arena that decides what the coop covers and who is paid for what. Implied by vna-whatcom-coop rather than drawn in it — which is itself the finding below.

nodes.label: BADGE ISSUANCE
nodes.note: From vna-sodoto-acceptance. The badge is not an operational act: it assigns a participant to a new position, someone who may now teach this. That is a POSITION RULE operating, which is why the file sits at collective-choice and spans down to operational.

nodes.label: CO-OP EXCHANGE
nodes.note: The operational half of hybrid-coop-money-and-value: goods, labour, price at the till, patronage. Every payoff here is set upstairs.

nodes.label: WHATCOM CARE
nodes.note: From vna-whatcom-coop. Six positions exchanging care, money, trust and situational knowledge. Operational: these choices directly affect tangible outcomes.

nodes.label: TEACH CHAIN
nodes.note: From sodoto-teach-chain-readings. Capability propagating between named participants. The bottleneck reading — remove the origin and the capability leaves — is a constitutional question this drawing raises but does not depict.

nodes.label: The constitutional band is empty. Nobody has drawn who may hold a seat.
nodes.note: In four drawings and 55 transactions there is not one statement about standing. For a project whose whole aim is people governing their own arrangements, that is the most interesting empty space on the canvas.

edges.label: undrawn
edges.note: who may sit here — No file of ours specifies standing for the plan-design arena.

edges.label: undrawn
edges.note: who may become a mentor — SODOTO assigns positions by badge, but nothing says who may enter the mentor position in the first place.

edges.label: → payoff rules
edges.note: sets PRICE and WAGE — The clearest adjacency we hold, and it is drawn inside a single file — which is how we discovered that file is two situations.

edges.label: → scope rules
edges.note: sets what is covered — Scope rules govern which outcomes a situation may produce. What the plan covers is exactly that.

edges.label: → position rules
edges.note: assigns who may teach — This is the adjacency that makes SODOTO an institution rather than a training programme.

edges.label: competence → issuance
edges.note: demonstrated competence triggers issuance — Adjacency runs both ways. The operational act supplies the input the collective-choice act needs, which is why the two cannot be separated cleanly.

edges.label: surplus → the split
edges.note: surplus to be split — The operational outcome that gives the board something to decide about.

edges.label: NO SEAT → boundary rule
edges.note: The CHW has no way up. In Ostrom's terms that is a boundary rule excluding a position from the arena that sets its payoff. CHW has no seat in plan design — ASSERTED, NOT OBSERVED. The red arrow from the Whatcom drawing, restated at the level where it belongs. If a CHW does sit in plan design, delete it.
